html:
In the Treaty of Tordesillas, signed in Castile on 7 June 1494, Spain and Portugal divided the lands outside Europe between them along a line running from pole to pole 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands.

After Columbus returned from his first voyage, the pope gave Spain the lands to the west. Portugal, which had pioneered the route around Africa, protested, and the two crowns agreed to move the line further west. Lands to the west were Spain's, lands to the east Portugal's.

The line cut across the eastern bulge of South America, which is why Brazil, reached by Cabral in 1500, speaks Portuguese. Other powers, such as England, France and the Netherlands, ignored the treaty. The two kingdoms later quarrelled over where the line ran on the other side of the world, in the Spice Islands. See Spain and Portugal.
sum: In the Treaty of Tordesillas, signed in Castile on 7 June 1494, Spain and Portugal divided the lands outside Europe between them along a line running from pole to pole 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands.
